title: Cohort-pairing mirror with deterministic replay and rollback crediting
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Motivation: We need a low-friction way to run paired A/B comparisons that guarantees deterministic post-failure replay and gives operators a fast recovery knob without losing telemetry fidelity. Current shadow/mirror flows copy traffic but do not maintain deterministic pairing, which complicates bisect and smoke-replay, and operators lack an accounting mechanism that prioritizes safe rollbacks after partial promotions. This change introduces a cohort-pairing mirror that binds requests across two variants (control/experiment) and a deterministic replay token that allows exact replay to either variant. Additionally we add a rollback-credit ledger: every successful micro-promote awards rollback credits to the experiment so that a single catastrophic regression can be compensated by consuming credits from lower-risk cohorts before triggering a global rollback.

Design summary: 1) Pairing layer in the router that annotates requests with a pairing_id and ensures deterministic hashing into cohort pairs. 2) Mirror engine that streams paired responses into the telemetry pipeline and writes compact replay records (event references + deterministic state fingerprint) to the replay store. 3) Replay worker capable of deterministic, time-bounded replays against specific model revisions to reproduce failures. 4) Rollback-credit ledger implemented as a lightweight in-cluster CRD-backed store with per-cohort balances and policies for credit consumption and top-ups. 5) Operator console additions: a cohort view showing pairing health, replay queue, and credit balance; a one-click freeze+replay action that creates a deterministic replay job and optionally drains credits to postpone rollback.

Checklist: - [x] Router pairing implementation (feature-flagged) - [x] Mirror engine + compact replay record format - [x] Replay worker + smoke-replay harness - [x] Rollback-credit ledger API + controller - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Runbook (docs/runbooks/rollback-crediting.md) - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts

Commits (high-level): commit 1: add pairing router and pairing_id propagation; commit 2: implement mirror engine and replay record serializer; commit 3: replay worker + deterministic replay harness; commit 4: rollback-credit ledger API and controller; commit 5: console: cohort balance view + action; commit 6: tests + runbook + docs; commit 7: small followups fixing race on ledger reconciliation.

Changed areas (high level): - internal/router/pairing_layer.go: new deterministic pairing and pairing_id propagation into headers - services/mirror/engine.go: mirror engine, buffering and write-to-replay-store - services/replay/worker.go: deterministic replay worker and CLI dry-run - controllers/rollback_credit_controller.go: CRD controller for credit ledger - docs/runbooks/rollback-crediting.md: operator runbook and example playbook - observability/dashboards/cohort_pairing.json: Grafana panel for pairing mismatch rates - tests/integration/cohort_pairing_test.go: integration tests for pairing + replay - docker/compose/ci-mock-replay.yaml: local replay harness config

Small code snippets in changed files (illustrative, not full diffs): - pairing_layer.go: ``// pairing id derived from user_id+route
hashPair := sha256(userID + route)
header.Set("X-Pairing-ID", hex.Encode(pair))`` - engine.go: ``record := &ReplayRecord{ PairID: pair, Control: respA.Summary(), Experiment: respB.Summary(), Fingerprint: modelState.Fingerprint() }
writer.Enqueue(record)`` - rollback_credit_controller.go: ``// consume credits atomically; returns false if insufficient
if !ledger.Consume(cohort, amount) { return ErrInsufficientCredits }``

Review conversation (summary): - Evan: "This is a neat approach; pairing avoids our nondeterministic sampling flakiness. Concern: replay records could blow up. How are we pruning them?" Priya: "Replay records are compact (pointer to request blob + three-line summary + fingerprint) and TTL'd at 7 days by default; we've added a GC job (controllers/replay_gc.go)." Evan: "SGTM; please add a perf test for GC"] - Marta: "Can we have a configurable escalation threshold that consumes credits only after N severity events?" Priya: "Added credit_policy.allow_delay, default 0, and tests to cover delayed consumption." Marta: "Approve after the docs + runbook link." - Will: "Found a race in controller reconciliation when ledger top-ups and consumption happen concurrently." Priya: "Fixed by adding reconciler transactions and added a unit test (ledger_reconcile_test.go)." Will: "Approved — good to merge."

CI summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration (mirrors + replay harness): initially failed on ledger race flake; fixed and rerun: pass - lint: pass - e2e smoke: pass

Merge: Squash merge after approvals; changelog entry added to release notes. Deployed behind feature-flag for 24 hours in canary, then ramped to 5% for paired cohorts across three test tenants.

Runbook excerpt (docs/runbooks/rollback-crediting.md): 1) If cohort pairing mismatch > 0.5% and replay failure reproduces, navigate to Console -> Cohorts -> <cohort> -> Freeze. 2) Click "Run deterministic replay" and select model revision(s); check replay job output for identical fingerprints. 3) If verified regression, check credit balance; if credits > threshold, choose "Consume credits and hold promotion" to allow rollback-free remediation window. 4) If credits insufficient, escalate to full rollback per standard rollback playbook.

Why this is unique: The crediting system decouples transient regressions from immediate rollbacks and gives SREs a principled, auditable way to prioritize recoveries. Deterministic pairing + replay significantly reduces noisy diffs when bisecting regressions across canary/AB lanes.
commits: feat(router): deterministic cohort pairing and pairing_id propagation
feat(mirror): paired mirror engine + compact replay record serializer
feat(replay): deterministic replay worker and dry-run CLI
feat(ledger): rollback-credit CRD + controller with atomic ops
test: integration tests for pairing, replay, ledger reconciliation
fix(ledger): reconciliation race guard and GC job for replay store
files_changed: internal/router/pairing_layer.go — new pairing layer and header propagation
services/mirror/engine.go — mirror engine + enqueue to replay store
services/replay/worker.go — deterministic replay worker and CLI
review_comments: Evan Zhou (2026-02-16): This addresses our non-deterministic sampling problem. Replay GC? We need bounds on storage usage.
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-16): Replay records are compact (pointer + 3-line summary) and TTL'd; added controllers/replay_gc.go and a perf test in tests/ci/replay_gc_test.go.
Marta Silva (2026-02-17): Add configurable delay before consuming credits so team can triage. Also include opt-out for certain tenants.
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-17): Added credit_policy.allow_delay and tenant opt-outs; tests updated.
Will Hart (2026-02-18): Found a race in ledger reconciliation under high concurrency.
Priya Nambiar (2026-02-19): Fixed with reconciler transaction and added ledger_reconcile_test.go; reran integration CI which passed.
release_notes: Introduce cohort-pairing mirror, deterministic replay store, and a rollback-credit ledger. Feature is behind a feature-flag; operators get runbook and console views. Improves reproducibility for canary/A-B workflows and gives teams a configurable crediting mechanism to delay rollbacks for low-severity regressions.
notes_for_ops: Deploy behind feature-flag. Start with canary tenant; monitor pairing_mismatch_rate and replay_queue_backlog. Default replay TTL is 7 days; GC job runs hourly. Credit ledger defaults: per-cohort starting balance 3 credits, top-up policy set via ENG-1899. If ledger shows negative balances, controller will emit alert 'rollback_credit_underflow' and pause auto-credit consumption.
postmerge_actions: 1) Enable feature-flag for canary for 24h. 2) Create dashboard alerts for pairing_mismatch_rate > 0.5% and replay_job_failure_rate > 1%. 3) Run internal training doc and a short demo for SREs. 4) Monitor storage for replay records for one week, consider reducing default TTL to 72h if pressure observed.
